Gas Turbine / CPP Hydraulic Pack (System 07)

Model: Multi-Layer Naval Machinery Diagnostic Transformer • Edge Quantized

CONFIDENCE 87%
MOST PROBABLE CONDITION IDENTIFIED

Cooling System Abnormality (Plate Heat Exchanger Flow Starvation)

Telemetry exhibits severe thermal bypass characteristics and high return line temperature gradient while under cruise propulsion load.

WHY WAS THIS FLAGGED?

  • Temperature above expected range: Recorded 485 °C / return temp +19 °C over nominal sea water benchmark.
  • Abnormal trend detected: Rate of rise exceeded 2.4 °C/min without corresponding shaft torque increase.
  • Similar previous fault found: High correlation (94%) with SAT-II historical fault record FLT-HIST-2025-1104.

PROBABLE CAUSES

  1. Cooling flow restriction: Silt/fouling in titanium plate heat exchanger seawater passes.
  2. Cooling system degradation: 3-way thermostatic bypass valve spool sticking in partial recirc mode.
  3. Sensor abnormality: Secondary RTD probe resistance drift or junction oxidation.

RECOMMENDED INITIAL CHECKS

1. Check cooling flow & measure differential pressure across seawater strainer.
2. Verify sensor reading using calibrated infrared optical pyrometer.
3. Inspect relevant cooling components, valve spindle free travel & seals.
4. Compare with previous maintenance record & check replacement part inventory.
